abstract: Understanding how lung alveolar type 2 (AT2) stem cells respond to chronic profibrotic insults in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is critical for developing therapies and determining physiological relevance of maladaptive regeneration. Using integrated snATAC/snRNA-sequencing of human lungs and in vitro models, we mapped distinct AT2 regenerative trajectories: resolvable euplastic repair and persistent dysplastic repair. Spatially restricted ITGB6/TGF{beta}1/SMAD3 signaling drives AT2-to-basaloid dysplasia via direct upregulation of KRT17 and Stratifin. Using murine models of dysplastic repair and a human precision-cut lung slice/stem cell incorporation assay, we show that KRT17 and its interaction with Stratifin are required for AT2 cell flattening, alveolar coverage, and barrier protection. AT2s leverage these mechanisms to re-epithelialize damaged tissue during chronic fibrosis, navigating a delicate balance between preventing further lung damage and driving aberrant epithelial remodeling. Collectively, we identify novel mechanisms governing alveolar metaplasia and its functional relevance, offering crucial insights for therapeutic interventions in fibrotic lung diseases.
